summary: Cohort signal loss during synchronized canary flip caused unpinned routing to quantized variant
description: Issue summary: During a synchronized canary roll for redwood-v1-large we observed that a small customer cohort lost explicit model pin state and was routed to the quantized variant (redwood-v1-large-q4). Impact: ~1400 requests over a 12m window returned lower-quality outputs and tokenization deltas; customer observed increased hallucination in 18% of affected responses (reported by customer and confirmed by telemetry). Environment: Dedicated tenant on prod:us-east-1. Steps to reproduce: 1) Start a weighted canary (10%) for redwood-v1-large across us-east-1 with prewarm enabled. 2) Trigger an orchestrator snapshot merge (scheduled merge job). 3) Send steady tenant traffic that relies on explicit version pin headers. Observed behaviour: A cohort of sessions lost model pin during the snapshot merge and were routed to redwood-v1-large-q4 (fallback path) instead of honoring tenant pin. Token counts and tokenizer fingerprints differed, leading to evaluation regression triggers from customer QA set. Expected behaviour: Tenant pin must be preserved across orchestrator snapshot merge; fallback routing should not select a different tokenizer family variant when pin is present. Relevant logs (trimmed): "2026-03-10T18:12:02Z control-plane: commit-snapshot nid=8792 merging epoch 412 -> 413" "2026-03-10T18:12:02Z orchestrator: cohort-signals: cohort=tn-998 lost-pin during merge window (prewarm=true)" "2026-03-10T18:12:03Z edge: route-resolver: selected target=redwood-v1-large-q4 weight=0.0->0.10" "2026-03-10T18:12:08Z serving-runtime: tokenization: tokenizer-hash mismatch from request header - expected 0x3b9f, got 0x8a2c" Additional notes: No 5xx spike, no autoscaler activity; issue correlates with coordinated snapshot/commit and edge prewarm probe timing jitter.

2026-03-10 18:40 - Priya Nair (SRE): Reproduced cohort loss in staging by forcing orchestrator snapshot merge during a prewarm window. Observed same edge route decision to q4 variant when pin header missing for ~12s.
2026-03-10 19:05 - Maya Chen (Customer Success): Confirmed with customer that they set explicit 'X-Model-Pin: redwood-v1-large' header; customer reports intermittent loss, not all requests affected.
2026-03-11 09:12 - Jordan Lee (Runtime): Tokenizer hashes differ between v1-large and v1-large-q4; should never be selected when pin present. Working on guard in route-resolver.

2026-03-12 11:30 - Priya Nair (SRE): Temporary mitigation deployed: route-resolver now verifies pin header at selection time and rejects fallback variants with differing tokenizer-family. Monitoring for false positives.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Orchestrator snapshot merge briefly cleared in-memory cohort pin map while control-plane applied new routing epoch, creating a window where edge route-resolver could not find a pinned mapping.

Hypothesis B: Edge prewarm probe timing (probe jitter ~30-50ms) caused a transient routing decision to include lower-cost q4 variant due to a race with weight application (weight transition 0.0->0.10).
Telemetry: Cohort loss aligns at 2026-03-10T18:12:02Z +/- 2s with snapshot commit event and prewarm probe spikes. No autoscaler preempt or GPU eviction recorded.
Control-plane review: commit-snapshot flow holds pin-delta writes, but a bug allowed a short-lived read-before-write window during epoch increments when prewarm flag true.
Edge analysis: route-resolver prioritizes explicit pin but falls back to best-available variant when lookup fails; it did not verify tokenizer-family equivalence before routing to quantized variant.

Repro: Deterministic in staging by inducing orchestrator merge while toggling prewarm and sending pinned header; reproduces cohort loss consistently when merge and first prewarm probe align within 60ms.
Customer impact: A subset of streaming chat sessions observed mixed-variant outputs; not all tenants affected because most flows had longer-lived pin leases (>30s).
resolution_notes: Mitigation steps taken: 1) Edge route-resolver patch rolled to prod (hotfix) that enforces: if a requested pin exists in header, reject candidate fallback variants where tokenizer-family != pinned model. 2) Control-plane commit-snapshot flow patched to serialize pin-map flush before epoch activation (PR merged: orchestrator#2147). 3) Deployed a short-term canary throttle to delay weight transitions by 200ms during snapshot commits to avoid the probe/merge race. Outcome: Customer reports quality metrics returned to baseline within 1 hour after hotfix. Follow-ups: add end-to-end unit test for pin-map visibility during snapshot commit, add telemetry to count pin-resolve-failures, update canary playbook to include snapshot coordination.
